body:
Thanks for the work.

I'll try to build from your fork tomorrow and test my plugin [Godot Doctor](https://github.com/codevogel/godot_doctor) with it.

I'm new to Editor PR's, but willing to work on this, so let me know if I can do anything else to help get this PR merged.

This seems to work flawlessly on my end. I've tested it with three separate projects running my plugin.

One improvement I could think of is emitting a signal `editor_ready` in `EditorPlugin` rather than only providing the `_editor_ready` hook. `EditorPlugin` signals are already emitted on editor hooks, e.g. `scene_saved` is a signal emitted from the plugin even though the editor is responsible for saving the scene, so I think it'd make sense to also emit `editor_ready` for those that prefer signals as hooks instead. 

If I'm correct, you added such a signal to be emitted internally in `EditorNode`, but `EditorPlugin` doesn't have access to `EditorNode`.

---

Just wanted to add some additional information on why we'd need this:

This PR would allow me to remove a bunch of hacky workaround code from my plugin;
https://github.com/codevogel/godot_doctor/blob/46574af5c8e348983c7e86d0a99340a2e38828cf/addons/godot_doctor/godot_doctor_plugin.gd#L541-L614

All this is necessary because `_set_window_layout` doesn't get called when there's no saved editor loadout, which is often the case when running from a CI runner. So currently I have to do a bunch of silly stuff like running the CLI on a separate thread, and setting a fallback timer for when `_set_window_layout` never gets called, to ensure that my plugin runs its validations only after the editor has fully initialized.

Adding this finally gives plugins an entry point to ensure that no code will execute before the editor is done doing stuff you have no control over.

>One improvement I could think of is emitting a signal editor_ready in EditorPlugin rather than only providing the _editor_ready hook. 

The signals in EditorPlugin are for observing events that can happen multiple times after the editor has already been initialized. The editor being ready is something that can only ever happen once, so I'm not seeing where using a signal for it would be appropriate.  

>If I'm correct, you added such a signal to be emitted internally in EditorNode, but EditorPlugin doesn't have access to EditorNode.

This was accidentally left over when I started making it a signal at first and then decided to make it a virtual.

> The signals in EditorPlugin are for observing events that can happen multiple times after the editor has already been initialized. The editor being ready is something that can only ever happen once, so I'm not seeing where using a signal for it would be appropriate.

Fair enough!
